problem: The Frank lead system is described as using eight electrodes. Frank's system uses seven: five around the chest at the fourth intercostal level, one on the back of the neck and one on the left leg. A ground electrode may be added, but that is not counted as a signal electrode.
fix: Write: "The Frank lead system uses seven electrodes (five around the chest, one on the back of the neck, one on the left leg), plus a ground electrode if used, to produce three orthogonal components X, Y and Z."

problem: "Z back to front" points the Z axis towards the front, but the standard Frank convention makes Z positive posteriorly (front to back). It also clashes with the parallel phrase "Y head to foot", which does match the standard Y polarity (positive downwards).
fix: Write: "X to the left (positive at the left), Y head to foot (positive at the foot), Z front to back (positive at the back)."

where: Section 3 table, Section 3 bullets, and Quiz Q7
problem: The table says QRS "0.06–0.10 s (up to 0.12 s)", the bullet calls a QRS "wider than 0.12 s" abnormal, but Q7 calls a QRS of exactly 0.12 s "a wide QRS". A student cannot tell whether 0.12 s is normal or wide.
fix: Use one boundary everywhere: "normal 0.06–0.10 s; 0.12 s is the borderline; ≥ 0.12 s is taken as wide". Change the bullet to "QRS of 0.12 s or more…" and Q7 to "3 mm is 0.12 s, at the borderline and conventionally called wide…".

problem: The caption says the ECG and VCG paths "share the same electrodes", and the diagram branches from the ECG electrodes straight into the Frank lead network. The Frank network needs its own electrodes at different body positions, so the diagram teaches a wrong connection.
fix: Caption: "…with a separate Frank electrode set feeding the VCG loop." Replace the edge elec → frank with a new node "Frank electrodes (7)" feeding "Frank lead network".

problem: "the QRS complex measures 2.0 mm across" is ambiguous, because amplitude is also measured in mm on the strip; a student can read it as a height of 2.0 mm.
fix: Write: "the QRS complex is 2.0 mm wide along the time axis".
